title: Volume of Cylinders, Cones and Spheres
seo_title: Grade 8 Volume Worksheets: Cylinders, Cones and Spheres (V = πr²h, ⅓πr²h, ⁴⁄₃πr³)
standard_text: Know the formulas for the volumes of cones, cylinders, and spheres and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 volume worksheets: find the volume of cylinders, cones and spheres in terms of π and with π ≈ 3.14, use diameters, find missing dimensions, and solve real-world problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Cylinder V = πr²h. Cone V = ⅓πr²h. Sphere V = ⁴⁄₃πr³.
key_sub: Use the radius, not the diameter. A cone holds one third of the cylinder with the same r and h.
body_html:
Three volume formulas

ShapeFormulaRemember
CylinderV = πr²harea of the circle × height
ConeV = ⅓πr²h⅓ of the cylinder with the same r and h
SphereV = ⁴⁄₃πr³r is cubed
Example

Find the volume of a cone with r = 3 cm and h = 4 cm.

V = ⅓ × π × 3² × 4.

= ⅓ × 36π = 12π.

Answer: 12π cm³ ≈ 37.68 cm³

Example

Find the volume of a sphere with diameter 6 m.

r = 6 ÷ 2 = 3.

V = ⁴⁄₃ × π × 27 = 36π.

Answer: 36π m³

Common mistakes

  • Using the diameter as the radius. Halve it first.
  • Forgetting the ⅓ for a cone.
  • Using r² instead of r³ for a sphere.
  • Writing square units. Volume is in cubic units (cm³).

faq.q: What is the formula for the volume of a cylinder?
faq.a: V = πr²h: the area of the circular base times the height.

faq.q: Why is the volume of a cone one third of a cylinder?
faq.a: A cone with the same radius and height as a cylinder holds exactly one third as much. Three cones of water fill the cylinder.

faq.q: What is the formula for the volume of a sphere?
faq.a: V = ⁴⁄₃πr³. For r = 3, V = ⁴⁄₃ × π × 27 = 36π.

faq.q: Should I leave π in the answer?
faq.a: Answers in terms of π (like 36π) are exact. If asked to use π ≈ 3.14, multiply to get a decimal.

items.e: 100π = π × r² × 4, so r² = 25 and r = 5 in.

items.q: Find the volume of a sphere with radius 3 m. Use π ≈ 3.14.

items.e: ⁴⁄₃πr³ = 36π, so r³ = 27 and r = 3 cm.

A cone has volume 12π cm³ and radius 3 cm. What is its height?
items.e: 12π = ⅓ × π × 9 × h = 3πh, so h = 4 cm.

items.e: 50π = ⅓ × π × r² × 6 = 2πr², so r² = 25 and r = 5 m.
